Rashi on Pesachim 39a:10:1.hebrew: מאי חסא - מאי טעמא קרינן ליה חסא? משום דזכר הוא דחס רחמנא עלן, אלמא להכי קיימא:
Rashi on Pesachim 39a:10:1.english: What is ḥassa - What is the reason we call it ḥassa? Because it is a reminder that the Merciful One had mercy [ḥas] on us; thus, it is designated for this [purpose].

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:10:2.english: Why are [the Egyptians] likened to bitter herbs - As it is written (Exodus 1:14): "And they embittered their lives."

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:10:3.hebrew: תחילה רכה - בתחילה נשתעבדו להן ע"י שכר, שהיו שוכרין אותן:
Rashi on Pesachim 39a:10:3.english: A soft beginning - At first [the Israelites] were subjugated to them through wages, for [the Egyptians] would hire them.

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:10:4.english: [A] bitter herb is hard at its end - Its stalk hardens like wood.

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:10:5.english: I retract - I will not [do so] again.

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:11:1.english: The bile of a kufya - The bile of a fish that is so named.

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:11:2.english: Like matzah - For they were juxtaposed [in Scripture].

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:11:3.hebrew: הירדוף - עץ שהמתיק בו משה את מי מרה, ואמרינן (בסוטה) (מכילתא פרשת בשלח): נס בתוך נס, שהוא היה מר, והוא הירדוף:
Rashi on Pesachim 39a:11:3.english: Oleander [hirduf] - A tree with which Moses sweetened the waters of Marah, and we say (in Sotah) (Mekhilta, Parashat Beshalach): [It was] a miracle within a miracle, for it was bitter — and that is oleander.

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:12:1.hebrew: הרזיפו - מין זרע וסם המות לבהמה הוא: הרזיפו אינו ניקח בכסף מעשר, דאינו פרי מאכל, ואנן אוכלא בעינן, דומיא דיין ושכר ובקר וצאן, כדכתיב (דברים י״ד:כ״ו) ונתתה הכסף בכל אשר תאוה נפשך וגו':
Rashi on Pesachim 39a:12:1.english: Harzipu - [It] is a type of seed and a deadly poison for animals. Harzipu cannot be purchased with [second-]tithe money, because it is not an edible fruit, and we require food, similar to wine, strong drink, cattle, and sheep, as it is written (Deuteronomy 14:26): "And you shall spend the money for whatever your soul desires, etc."

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:13:1.hebrew: ואימא מרור חד - מינא הוא מהנך ירקות, ולאו כל הני, אלא מר שבכולן:
Rashi on Pesachim 39a:13:1.english: And say [that] bitter herb [is] one - It is [only] one species of those vegetables, and not all of these, rather [only] the most bitter of all of them.

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:15:3.hebrew: והרמוצה - מין דלעת הוא, ובמסכת נדרים (דף נא.) מפ': קרא קרקוזאי:
Rashi on Pesachim 39a:15:3.english: And the harmutza - It is a type of gourd, and in Tractate Nedarim (51a) [the Gemara] explains [that it is] kara karkozai [a Karkozai gourd].

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:16:1.hebrew: וכי תימא כולהו בהדי הדדי קתני - דבכל הני קאמר דאינן כלאים זה בזה — חזרת, עולשין וכרישין:
Rashi on Pesachim 39a:16:1.english: And if you say [that] it teaches all of them together - [Meaning] that regarding all of these it says that they are not kilayim [diverse kinds] with one another — lettuce, endives, and leeks.

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:16:2.hebrew: זוגות זוגות - חזרת וחזרת גלין, או עולשין ועולשי שדה, וכן כולן שנינו דאין כלאים זה בזה, אבל חזרת בעולשין — לא:
Rashi on Pesachim 39a:16:2.english: In pairs - Lettuce and wild lettuce [*chazeret galin*], or endives and field endives, and similarly [for] all of them, we learned [in the Mishnah] that they are not *kilayim* [forbidden mixtures] with one another; but lettuce with endives — no.

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:17:1.hebrew: מאי - כולן נזרעין בערוגה אחת דאמר רב לעיל? נזרעין כהלכתן קא אמר, כדי שלא יינקו זה מזה, כגון חמשה זרעונין בערוגה של ששה על ששה טפחים, כדתנן במסכת שבת (דף פד:):
Rashi on Pesachim 39a:17:1.english: What - [does] "all of them may be planted in one garden bed" that Rav said above [mean]? He meant [that] they may be planted in their proper manner, so that they do not draw nourishment from one another — for example, five seeds in a garden bed of six by six handbreadths, as we learned in a Mishnah in Tractate Shabbat (84b).

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:1:1.hebrew: אלו ירקות שאדם יוצא בהן ידי חובתו בחזרת ובתמכא ובעולשי' ובחרחבינא ובמרור - כולהו מפרש בגמ':
Rashi on Pesachim 39a:1:1.english: These are the vegetables with which a person fulfills his obligation: with chazeret, and with tamkha, and with olashin, and with charchavina, and with maror - All of them are explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:1:3.english: Over-boiled - Boiled very much until they dissolve.

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:1:4.english: Cooked - In the [ordinary] manner of cooking.

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:2:1.hebrew: ומצטרפין לכזית - אם אין לו מאחד מהן כזית, אבל יש לו מזה חצי זית ומזה חצי זית, מצטרפין זה עם זה כדי לצאת ידי חובתו:
Rashi on Pesachim 39a:2:1.english: And they join together to [the measure of] an olive-bulk - If he does not have an olive-bulk from one of them, but he has half an olive[-bulk] from this [one] and half an olive[-bulk] from that [one], they join together with one another in order to fulfill his obligation.

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:2:2.hebrew: ובדמאי ובמעשר ראשון כו' - אבל בטבל לא, ואף על גב דמעשר ירק דרבנן, הויא לה מצוה הבאה בעבירה, דומיא דעציץ שאינו נקוב דאמרן בפירקין:
Rashi on Pesachim 39a:2:2.english: And with demai, and with first tithe, etc. - But not with tevel [untithed produce]; and even though the tithe of vegetables is rabbinic, it is [considered] a mitzvah that comes through a transgression, similar to [the case of] an unperforated pot that we stated [earlier] in our chapter.

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:3:2.english: Hindevi - An herb that is called crespele [in Old French, i.e., curly endive].

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:3:4.hebrew: אצוותא דדיקלא - סיב הגדל ונכרך סביב לדקל, שקורין ווידיל"א:
Rashi on Pesachim 39a:3:4.english: Atzvata dedikla - A fibrous [creeper] that grows and wraps around the palm tree, which they call vedille [bindweed, in Old French].

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:3:5.english: Meraryata - [In Old French,] amerfoil, and it is [also called] poprez.

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:4:1.english: Charchallin - Its name has not been explained.

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:4:3.hebrew: עולשי שדה - אע"ג דיש להן שם לווי, הרי הן כעולשי גינה:
Rashi on Pesachim 39a:4:3.english: Wild endives - Even though they have a qualifying name, they are like garden endives.

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:5:1.english: Asvas, and tura, and mar yeroah - [These are] kinds of vegetables.

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:6:2.english: Ḥazeret gallim - It is an accompanying [descriptive] name.

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:7:1.hebrew: ערקבלין - מפרש בסוף פ' שני דעירובין: אצוותא חרזייתא. הוא סיב גדול ועב, ומין לעצמו הוא:
Rashi on Pesachim 39a:7:1.english: Arkablin - It is explained at the end of the second chapter of Eruvin [that it is] atzvata charzayyata [prickly palm-ivy]; it is a large and thick fibrous bast, and it is a species unto itself.

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:7:2.hebrew: וחזרתי על כל תלמידיו - של ר' אליעזר, ובקשתי לי חבר לסייעני ששמע דבר זה מפיו, ולא מצאתי:
Rashi on Pesachim 39a:7:2.english: And I went around all of his students - of Rabbi Eliezer, and I sought for myself a colleague to assist me who had heard this matter from his mouth, and I did not find [one].

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:8:1.hebrew: כל ירק מר - תרווייהו אית ליה: יש לו שרף ופניו מכסיפין, והן הן סימני מרור:
Rashi on Pesachim 39a:8:1.english: Any bitter herb - It has both [of them]: it has sap and its surface is pale, and these are the signs of maror.

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:8:2.hebrew: שרף - כשסוחטין אותו במקום חיתוכו, יוצא ממנו שרף לבן כחלב, וקורין לייטו"ן:
Rashi on Pesachim 39a:8:2.english: Sap - When one squeezes it at the place where it is cut, a white sap like milk comes out of it, and they call [it] laitun [Old French: milky sap].

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:8:3.hebrew: מכסיפין - אינו ירק מאד ככרתי, אלא פלד"ש:
Rashi on Pesachim 39a:8:3.english: [Whose surface] turns pale - It is not very green like leeks, rather [it is] pale [Old French: pales].

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:8:4.hebrew: מדברי כולן - כל המפרשין שמות הירקות — כגון מתני' ותנא דבר קפרא ורבי יהודה ור' מאיר ותנא דבי שמואל — מכולן למדנו שהמרור יש לו שרף ופניו מכסיפין, שבכל הירקות הללו רואין אנו בהן הסימנין האלו:
Rashi on Pesachim 39a:8:4.english: From the statements of all of them - All those who specify the names of the vegetables — such as the Mishnah, the Tanna of [the school of] Bar Kappara, Rabbi Yehuda, Rabbi Meir, and the Tanna of the school of Shmuel — from all of them we learn that maror [bitter herbs] has sap and its surface turns pale, for in all of these vegetables we see these characteristics.

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:9:1.english: For merirata - Popretz [Old French for a type of bitter herb].

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:9:2.english: But - We learned chazeret [as] the first of all of them.

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:9:3.hebrew: ותנא דבי שמואל - נמי חזרת תנא ברישא, אלמא היא קדמי לכולהו:
Rashi on Pesachim 39a:9:3.english: And [a Sage of] the school of Shmuel taught - [he] also taught ḥazeret first; thus, it precedes all of them.

Rashi on Pesachim 39a:9:4.hebrew: מצוה בחזרת - כדמפרש טעמא כדרבא ור' יונתן:
Rashi on Pesachim 39a:9:4.english: The mitzvah is with chazeret - As [the Gemara] explains the reason, according to Rava and Rabbi Yonatan.

Tosafot on Pesachim 39a:11:1.hebrew: ואימא הירדוף כי מצה וכו' - בפ' לולב הגזול (סוכה דף לב:) פריך גבי הדס: "ואימא הירדוף"? אמר אביי: "דרכי' דרכי נועם". ופ"ה דלא הוי נועם, כיון דהוי סם המות לבהמה. הכא נמי ה"מ לשנויי הכי, אלא דמשני שפיר טפי. אבל קשה לרשב"א: דלעיל אמר דהירדופני כשר למרור, ובפרק אלו טרפות (חולין דף נח:) משמע דהוי סם המות לבהמה — דאמר: בהמה שאכלה הירדופני כשירה, ופריך: היינו הירדפוני היינו סם המות? ומשני: תרי גווני סם המות:
Tosafot on Pesachim 39a:11:1.english: "And say [perhaps] oleander (hirduf) — like matza, etc." - In the chapter [entitled] Lulav HaGazul (Sukkah 32b), [the Gemara] asks regarding the myrtle (hadas): "And say [perhaps] oleander (hirduf)?" Abaye said: "[The Torah's] ways are ways of pleasantness" [Proverbs 3:17]. And Rashi explained that it is not pleasant, since it is a deadly poison for an animal. Here too, [the Gemara] could have answered thus, except that it gives a better answer. However, it is difficult for the Rashba: for earlier [the Gemara] said that hirdufni (oleander) is valid for maror, whereas in the chapter [entitled] Eilu Tereifot (Chullin 58b), it is implied that it is a deadly poison for an animal — for it says: "An animal that ate hirdufni is kosher," and [the Gemara] asks: "Isn't hirdufni the same as deadly poison?" And it answers: "There are two types of deadly poison."

Tosafot on Pesachim 39a:3:1.hebrew: אצוותא דדיקלא - צ"ל דהוי מין זרעים, דהא לקמן אמרינן: "מה מצה מין זרעים, אף מרור מין זרעים":
Tosafot on Pesachim 39a:3:1.english: Atzvota dedikla [the plant around the palm tree] - One must say that it is a species of seed-bearing plants, for later [the Gemara] says: "Just as matzah is a species of seed-bearing plants, so too maror is a species of seed-bearing plants."
